manifesto.p1: You know how to build it. You just shouldn’t have to.
manifesto.p2: Every SaaS demands the same plumbing: auth, billing, multi‑tenancy, an admin. Those first 300+ hours are not what makes your product valuable. That work is already written and already tested. What is left is the part only you can build.

cli.title: Pick your stack. Run one command.
cli.lead: Most starter kits ship every permutation at once and leave you deleting the parts you did not ask for. This one asks twelve questions and writes only the answers, so a single-tenant project never carries multi-tenant code and nothing in the repository is dead on arrival.

unavailable.elysia: Elysia targets Bun. Deploy to Vercel or self-host, or pick Hono.

unavailable.sqlite: SQLite needs a persistent filesystem or a D1 binding. Deploy to Cloudflare or self-host.

unavailable.bun: Cloudflare runs Workers, not Bun. Deploy to Vercel or self-host.

unavailable.d1: D1 is a Cloudflare binding. Deploy to Cloudflare to use it.
unavailable.file: A local file needs a disk that survives a deploy. Self-host to use it.

unavailable.commerce: A store needs something to charge with. Pick a billing provider first.
unavailable.courses: A subscription course needs something to charge with. Pick a billing provider first.
unavailable.post-editor: There is nothing to edit without MDX content. Turn content on first.

cli.choicesLabel: Every answer rewrites the flags. Copy the command when it matches your architecture.

reuse.title: The second project costs you nothing.
reuse.body: Run the CLI again with different answers. What changes is the stack. What remains is the test suite, the clean architecture, and the <accent>lifetime updates</accent> you already paid for.

line.title: The strong foundation
line.description: Four things every SaaS needs on day one. Every one of them already runs, and every one of them is work you are not doing.

auth.title: Own your data. Protect your margins.
auth.body: Better Auth runs on your own database instead of per-user pricing that scales against you. Your user table, your sessions, your margins. The bill at 50,000 monthly actives is the same as the bill at 50, and it is zero either way.

tests.title: Know it works before you merge.
tests.body: Not vibe-coded on a weekend. 176 test files and 8 Playwright suites run on every pull request, and the coverage gate fails the build before anything broken can merge. Deploy on a Friday and actually take the weekend.

i18n.title: Sell in 9 languages without a rewrite.
i18n.body: Locale routing, translations, timezones and currency formatting are native to the codebase, not bolted on. A nine-language catalogue with 195 timezones and 156 currencies is configured before you write a line, and a parity check fails the build the moment a translation goes missing.

edge.title: Your architecture, not someone else's.
edge.body: The CLI asks what you are building and scaffolds that, instead of handing you one opinionated shape to fight. Vite+ and TanStack Start underneath: instant HMR and strict types while you work, a runtime built for the edge once you ship.

quality.title: Quality control
quality.body: Every unit, integration and end-to-end path is covered before it merges. 176 test files, 8 Playwright suites in real Chromium and WebKit, and a coverage gate that runs on every pull request and every push to main.
quality.consequence: Which is what makes an agent safe to run here. It can write as fast as it likes; nothing it breaks reaches main, and you find out at the pull request instead of in production.

faq.title: Straight answers
faq.lead: The questions buyers actually ask, answered in full. If yours is not here, send it over.
faq.contact: Ask the engineer who built it

q1.question: What exactly do I get?
q1.answer: A licence to the proprietary CLI, which generates a SaaS application with TanStack Start, React, Vite+, Better Auth, Drizzle with Cloudflare D1, Polar, Resend and use-intl. You receive editable application source, tests, the visual page designer and documentation. Sign in after purchase to obtain the key required to install and use the CLI. Complete and Agency add the advertised learning and design material; Agency also covers client projects.

q2.question: Why Better Auth instead of Clerk or Auth0?
q2.answer: Ownership. Hosted auth charges you per monthly active user, which means your costs scale exactly when your revenue should. Better Auth lives in your codebase and your database. Your users are rows you own, not line items on someone else's invoice.

q3.question: Is it really 100% test coverage?
q3.answer: Yes. Statements, branches, functions and lines under Vitest, plus Playwright end-to-end suites running in real Chromium and WebKit. Coverage is enforced as a CI gate on every pull request, not reported as a screenshot. The coverage summary is generated by this public website repository.

q4.question: How do I know it is what this page says it is?
q4.answer: Inspect the public documentation and repository before you buy. You can request a refund before delivery of separate paid material; the Refunds page explains the process. Mandatory cancellation rights and remedies for faulty or undelivered content remain protected.

q5.question: Why not just have an AI agent build this?
q5.answer: It will, and the result will look right. What it will not tell you is which of the auth edge cases it skipped, which webhook is not idempotent, or that the i18n parity check it never wrote would have caught the missing key. Generated code is the cheap part now. The expensive part is the gate that proves it is correct, and that is what this repository is: point an agent at it and it inherits 176 test files, strict types and a build that fails when it is wrong.

q6.question: Do I need the Complete tier?
q6.answer: Core gives you the machine. Complete adds the reasoning and the support around it: the full video course from empty folder to production, a walkthrough of every module, priority replies within one business day, and free lifetime access to reactprojects.com. Most buyers take Complete, because the code is the cheap part.

q7.question: Is any of this a subscription?
q7.answer: No. You pay once. Lifetime core updates are included, the code sits in your repository, and there is no seat count, no monthly active user meter and no renewal date.

q8.question: What does “lifetime updates” cover?
q8.answer: Every update to the core codebase, including framework upgrades, new modules and security patches, for as long as SaaSyLand exists. You buy once and the machine keeps getting better.

q9.question: Can I use it for client work?
q9.answer: Core and Complete cover unlimited generated applications for your own products; Agency also covers client projects. The private CLI requires a purchase and valid key and cannot be modified or redistributed, subject to mandatory legal exceptions. You may edit and deploy generated applications. This public website and previous MIT releases remain MIT licensed.

q10.question: Why trust a starter kit built by one engineer?
q10.answer: Because the claims are checkable. The coverage report is generated by the repository, the CI workflow that enforces it is in the repository, and the person who wrote it builds production software for a living. Read the documentation before you pay and hold this page to it.

q11.question: Do I need to know Vite+ and TanStack Start?
q11.answer: No. If you know React and TypeScript, you can read the code from day one. TanStack Start handles routing and server functions, Vite+ provides the development tools, and the application runs on Cloudflare Workers. The masterclass covers the whole flow step by step.
